heroHeadline: JNIM Storms 'Africa's Alcatraz' Prison 60km from Bamako; Supply Convoys Burned as Siege Tactics Reinstated
heroSubtitle: On May 6–7, 2026, JNIM fighters assaulted the Kenieroba Central Prison — Mali's maximum-security facility southwest of Bamako housing 2,500 inmates including 72+ high-value JNIM detainees captured after the April 25 nationwide offensive. Simultaneously, JNIM burned food supply convoys heading to Bamako and established new checkpoints around the capital, reinstating the supply siege that the May 2 convoy of 800+ trucks had broken. FAMa is repelling the prison assault. Niger and AES forces separately reported eliminating 150+ militants and freeing captured soldiers in a Tillabéri operation on May 6. Burkina Faso's junta suspended French broadcaster TV5Monde for alleged 'disinformation,' extending its systematic media crackdown documented by HRW. The UN OHCHR's 'gravely concerning' designation for extrajudicial killings in post-offensive Mali remains in force, and the junta's information embargo prevents independent verification across all northern and central conflict zones.
footerNote: Data sourced from ACLED, RFI, Le Monde, Crisis Group, UN OHCHR, HRW, SIPRI, AFP, Bloomberg, Al Jazeera, Reuters, Long War Journal, Africa Center for Strategic Studies, Institute for Economics & Peace, US Embassy Bamako, FAO, WFP, Chatham House, PBS NewsHour, Manila Times, GlobalSecurity.org, and Pravda Burkina Faso. All figures approximate unless stated.
